episode.title: Preserve the previously focused terminal when closing a programmatically managed diff tab
episode.before: At parent commit 196c772a970166a26fa0e5f92f4fbd89ec265301, the shared diff-closing routine found the matching diff tab and called the editor API as close(tab), without the keep-focus argument. The same routine was used by direct close, accept, and cancel paths, so closing an accepted or rejected diff could move focus from the terminal to an editor.
episode.after: At commit e5b6680332883bd72aaa59292936b184f340256f, the shared routine calls close(tab, true), preserving the focus held outside the diff while retaining existing context reset, tracked-content cleanup, and accept/reject notification behavior. Unit tests assert the keep-focus argument across close, accept, and cancel paths, while an extension-host integration test focuses a terminal, opens and accepts a diff, and verifies that a typing probe does not reach the previously opened editor. The integration test is built, launched through the editor test harness, and added to CI.
episode.diff: The behavioral implementation is a one-argument change in the shared diff-tab cleanup boundary: the matched tab is closed with keepFocus=true. Supporting changes add comprehensive unit coverage and a reusable editor mock, expose a development-only command for opening a diff during extension-host tests, bundle and launch the new integration tests, add the editor test dependency and scripts, and execute the suite in CI under a virtual display on Linux.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned resolution is commit e5b6680332883bd72aaa59292936b184f340256f, titled "fix(vscode-ide-companion): preserve terminal focus when closing diff tabs (#29378)", with parent 196c772a970166a26fa0e5f92f4fbd89ec265301.

evidence_units.claim: The parent implementation closed a matched diff tab with close(tab), supplying no keep-focus argument.
The implementation changes the matched-tab close call from close(tab) to close(tab, true).

Before closing the tab, the shared routine clears the diff-visible context and removes tracked diff metadata and generated content; it then closes only the tab whose modified URI matches the requested diff URI, now with keepFocus=true.
Both accepting and cancelling a diff invoke the shared close routine; after cleanup they preserve their existing accepted or rejected protocol notifications for tracked diffs.
Closing a diff by original file path also resolves the tracked modified-document URI and invokes the same shared close routine.

Unit tests require direct close, accept, and cancel paths to call the tab-closing API with the matched tab and true, while also checking visibility reset, content cleanup, notifications, and missing-state behavior.

The extension-host regression test activates the extension, focuses a terminal, opens a diff, accepts it, sends a default typing command, and fails if the probe text appears in the previously opened dummy editor; absence of that text is the focus-preservation oracle.

A non-production command was added to open a diff with supplied file path and content, giving the extension-host regression test a controlled entry point without exposing that command in production mode.
The integration runner loads the focus test inside the extension host, and the launcher uses the editor test harness with other extensions disabled.
The repository wires the editor integration suite into the root and package scripts and runs it in CI, using xvfb-run on Linux.

candidate_atomics.name: close-managed-diff-with-focus-preservation
candidate_atomics.title: Close a managed diff without stealing focus
candidate_atomics.description: At the shared diff-tab cleanup boundary, close the exact matching diff tab with the editor API's keep-focus option while retaining visibility-state reset, generated-content cleanup, and existing accept/reject outcomes.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent completion of a diff review from redirecting keyboard focus away from the terminal or other surface the user was actively using.
semantic_action.module_role: Managed diff lifecycle and tab cleanup owner
semantic_action.pre_state: A managed diff has a tracked modified-document URI, its matching diff tab is open, and another UI surface may currently own focus.
semantic_action.post_state: The matching diff tab is closed and its tracked state is cleaned up, while the previously focused UI surface remains focused and accept/reject protocol behavior is unchanged.
semantic_action.validation: Unit assertions observe close(matchedTab, true) for direct close, accept, and cancel paths and also verify context reset, content cleanup, notifications, and graceful missing-state handling.

semantic_action.intent: Detect focus regressions that cannot be established solely from mocked API-call assertions.

candidate_workflows.name: preserve-focus-across-programmatic-diff-closure
candidate_workflows.title: Preserve user focus when programmatically closing a review diff
candidate_workflows.description: Resolve a review-navigation regression by applying focus preservation at the shared tab-close boundary, checking every completion path that uses it, and validating the observable result inside a real editor host.

workflow_graph.goal: Closing, accepting, or cancelling a managed diff removes the intended review tab and associated state without moving keyboard focus from the terminal or another previously focused surface.
when_to_use: A programmatically closed diff or review tab causes focus to jump to an editor or another unintended surface.
Several diff-completion entry points converge on one shared tab-closing routine.
The host editor exposes a close option that retains the current focus owner and supports extension-host behavioral tests.
anti_goals: Do not change how diff content is accepted, rejected, or transmitted.
Do not keep the diff tab open merely to avoid the focus transition.
Do not expose test-only diff-opening controls in production mode.
Do not treat mocked API assertions alone as proof of real focus routing.
not_applicable_when: The review surface is not a host-editor tab or its close API has no focus-preservation capability.
The desired product behavior is to focus a specific editor after the review closes.
No reproducible completion path or behavioral focus oracle can be established.
inputs: A reproducible sequence that focuses a non-diff surface, opens a managed diff, and completes it
The shared lifecycle routine that identifies and closes the managed diff tab
The host API contract for preserving focus during tab closure
An extension-host test launcher capable of issuing commands and observing input routing
workflow_graph.entry_state: A managed diff can be opened and completed, but its shared close call omits focus preservation, allowing the host to redirect focus after the tab disappears.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Every relevant completion path reaches a shared keep-focus close operation, tracked diff state is still reconciled, protocol outcomes remain intact, and an automated real-host test demonstrates that keyboard input is not redirected to the editor.

steps.condition: Use when the affected close, accept, and cancel paths share the same matched-tab cleanup boundary.
steps.validation: Assert that each supported completion path closes the exact matched diff tab with keepFocus=true and preserves its existing cleanup and notification contract.

steps.condition: Run when an editor-host harness can establish terminal focus, invoke the managed-diff lifecycle, and probe input routing.
steps.validation: After accepting the diff, issue a typing command and require that the previously opened editor document does not contain the probe text; execute this oracle in CI.

validation_ladder: Inspect the parent and changed implementation to confirm the focus regression is localized to the shared matched-tab close call.
Run unit tests covering direct close, accept, and cancel, requiring the keep-focus argument plus unchanged state cleanup and notifications.
Run the extension-host scenario that focuses a terminal, accepts a diff, and verifies a typing probe does not reach the editor.
Run the editor integration suite in CI, with a virtual display where required by the operating system.
stop_conditions: Stop if close, accept, and cancel do not converge on the same lifecycle boundary; model and validate their distinct owners separately.
Stop if the host close API cannot retain focus or if product requirements explicitly require focusing another surface.
Do not claim completion if only the close-call mock passes and no real-host focus-routing oracle is available.
Stop if preserving focus breaks diff-state cleanup or accepted/rejected notification behavior.
